objective_interpretation: The review treats the site as a proof-and-findability decision for a prospect evaluating advisors, not as a general brand review.

activated_modules.reason: How the firm frames its specialism against comparable firms is a positioning choice.
A prospective client and a referral source weigh the same site differently.
The site has to justify why this firm, not just state what it does.
A prospect choosing an advisor compares this firm against others they could engage.
The advisory service itself, and how its scope is described, is the subject of the enquiry decision.
Published case studies and articles are how the firm demonstrates expertise before a first call.
A track record and named client outcomes are what a prospect weighs before reaching out.
A prospect who does not already know the firm’s name has to be able to find it.
The site is what a prospect lands on before ever making contact.
Submitting an enquiry is the action this review exists to increase.
The site is a set of web pages.
What referral sources and past clients say publicly bears directly on a prospect’s decision to reach out.

dormant_modules.reason: Broader advisory-market trends are not what this quarter’s enquiry decision turns on.
Engagement rates are quoted per client, not published, so there is no price to analyse on the site.
No compliance driver was raised for this specific site.
No security, privacy or compliance concern was raised for this decision.
Engagement delivery is out of scope for a site-and-enquiry decision.
No regulatory or macro-economic driver bears on this decision.

comparison_plan.rationale: No comparisons were supplied, so the qualified set had to be discovered by specialism.

anticipated_gaps: No analytics access, so where a referred prospect first lands on the site is not directly observable.
